subtype: Approach: past-paper practice and error log [Action]
passage: My name is Vaibhav, and I used to say I lost marks "because Maths is hard". That was too vague to fix. So I printed eight previous years of board papers and solved them one by one with the clock running and my phone in another room. After marking each paper I made a table: every lost mark got a cause, either careless slip, concept I did not know, or slow writing. When I added it up, careless slips were the biggest column by far, bigger than the concepts. Zubin, my study partner, laughed: "You have been blaming the wrong thing." Since then I read every answer line by line in the last ten minutes, and my next paper lost noticeably fewer marks.

qa.q: How many previous years of board papers did Vaibhav solve?
qa.a: Vaibhav solved eight previous years of board papers.

qa.q: What did Vaibhav feel when careless slips turned out to be the biggest column?
qa.a: Surprised, since Vaibhav had blamed Maths being hard, and probably relieved that careless slips can be fixed.

qa.q: What could Vaibhav do if slow writing becomes the next biggest cause?
qa.a: Practise timed answers and cut out extra words, because targeting the largest cause each time keeps the effort useful.

qa.q: How might Zubin see the finding?
qa.a: With amusement and some admiration, since Zubin laughed and said Vaibhav had been blaming the wrong thing.

grounding: Vaibhav solves eight years of board papers under time, logs every lost mark by cause, and targets the largest cause.

Tuition notes: Reena, Class 10 Maths, 20 February
Over the last three weeks Reena has sat all eight past board papers from 2016 to 2023, one every two or three days, with a timer on my desk. After each one we marked it together and she wrote every lost mark in a small notebook with its reason: careless slip, didn't know the concept, ran out of time. Today she added up the columns. Careless slips: 31 marks. Concepts: 9. Time: 6. She stared at the numbers and said, "So I actually know it. I'm just throwing it away." She looked annoyed and relieved at once. For the next two weeks we will work on checking habits: re-reading signs, copying numbers carefully and a five-minute check at the end.
— Aparna

qa.q: How many marks did Reena lose to careless slips?
qa.a: She lost 31 marks to careless slips.

qa.q: What did Reena feel when she saw the totals?
qa.a: She felt annoyed at throwing marks away, but relieved to learn that she actually knew most of the Maths.

qa.q: Why is working on careless slips a good next step for Reena?
qa.a: It is by far the largest cause, 31 marks against 9 and 6, so better checking habits will win back more marks than studying new concepts.

qa.q: How does Aparna see the error log?
qa.a: Aparna treats it as a map for the next two weeks, turning Reena's lost marks into a clear focus on checking habits.

grounding: A tutor's note shows a student doing eight timed past papers, logging lost marks by cause and targeting the biggest one.

Sunday night
Finished the last of the eight Science board papers today, the 2016 one, timed, at the dining table while Jasleen did hers on a video call. Then I did what Sir told us: added up my lost marks by reason. I've been writing each one at the back of my rough book since January. Totals: slow writing, 38. Didn't know the concept, 14. Careless, 11. I always thought my problem was not knowing enough. It isn't. I'm running out of time on the five-mark answers because I write essays when points would do. New plan: every day this week, three long answers in point form against a timer, eight minutes each. Jasleen says she'll time me. Strange to feel relieved about 38 lost marks, but I do.
Kalyani

qa.q: Which paper did Kalyani finish today?
qa.a: The 2016 Science paper, the last of the eight.

qa.q: Why does Kalyani feel relieved about 38 lost marks?
qa.a: Kalyani now knows the biggest cause is slow writing, which feels fixable, and is less worried about not knowing enough.

qa.q: What else could Kalyani do to fix slow writing?
qa.a: Study how marking schemes award points and practise matching them, so each long answer covers the key points in fewer words.

qa.q: What is it like for Jasleen to time Kalyani's answers?
qa.a: Jasleen gets to support a friend and may pick up the same point-form habit for her own papers.

grounding: A student's diary shows timed past papers and a lost-marks log revealing slow writing as the largest cause to target.
